causal_findings: A real PostgreSQL pg_stat_activity Lock wait is witnessed for the exact child backend PID, backend_start and application_name, with only the owned blocker PID returned by pg_blocking_pids.

Raw phase messages preserve application_lock, natural outcome, then settled-session ordering. Both natural errors are SQLSTATE 55P03 and occur before the 5-second statement guard, not a fixture cancellation or helper teardown.

The exact source asserts the parent blocker transaction remains active and checks its original PID after the natural outcome, before explicit rollback; the passing JUnit binds these assertions. This continued-lock claim uses source plus execution and is not presented as a nonexistent extra receipt field.

The same physical child connection, backend PID, backend_start and application_name persist through all phases; transaction-local lock_timeout restores to 0 or 500ms as configured, and statement_timeout stays 5000 ms.
Durable operation/application/audit snapshots after the timeout equal their pre-attempt snapshots. The exact source's NOWAIT operation-row acquisition also succeeds before the blocker is released.

After explicit blocker release, recovery returns 1, completes the confirmed mock operation once, preserves attempt 1 / retry 2 and the application, and creates exactly one LEASE_RECOVERY audit. A repeated sweep returns 0 with identical durable state.

The production receipt is recorded before fixture release/stop/drop cleanup; the separate cleanup receipt reports helper exited=true, exit code 0, no forced actions and no blocker-release error in both cases.
qualification.supported_inference: On this disposable PostgreSQL 17 / psycopg 3 run, the published recover_expired change applies a 1000 ms transaction-local timeout to this secondary application-row lock acquisition while preserving an existing stricter 500 ms setting. The natural elapsed outcomes were 1.011152009 s and 0.511210303 s, respectively. The failed transaction rolls back without durable mutation, connection settings restore, and later recovery succeeds once and remains idempotent.
